Package options reference

Source: vignettes/package-options.Rmd
package-options.Rmd

What package options are for

Package options control settings shared by the whole R process, including network timeouts and diagnostic logging. oauth_client() and oauth_module_server() arguments apply to one app registration or module. The Usage guide covers login setup.

Set an option at app startup

For example, give a slow provider up to ten seconds per network request. Put this near the top of app.R, before creating the provider and client:

options(shinyOAuth.timeout = 10)

A longer timeout gives a slow provider more time to respond, but delays failure when the service is unavailable. Restore the default with options(shinyOAuth.timeout = NULL).

Options affect every session sharing that R process; they are app-wide settings rather than per-user settings.

Times use seconds unless a setting explicitly says milliseconds.

Logging

These options control diagnostic events and the request details they contain.

  • options(shinyOAuth.audit_hook = function(event){ ... }) – receive structured audit and error events

  • options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_http = FALSE) – exclude HTTP request details from audit events (default: TRUE)

  • options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_raw_session_token = TRUE) – include the raw shiny_session[["token"]] in native audit-hook payloads. By default, hooks receive only shiny_session[["session_token_digest"]]

  • options(shinyOAuth.audit_redact_http = FALSE) – disable automatic redaction of sensitive data in audit events (default: TRUE). Debug only: raw mode can expose cookies, authorization headers, codes, state values, and client IP addresses

  • options(shinyOAuth.telemetry_path_scrubber = function(path) NULL) – return approved route labels for audit and OTel paths, which are omitted by default. Return NULL for unknown routes, remove identifying segments, and make the function idempotent.

  • options(shinyOAuth.audit_digest_key = ...) – shared HMAC-SHA256 key of at least 32 bytes for audit/OTel correlation. The default is a random per-process key; invalid configured keys cause an error.

  • options(shinyOAuth.otel_tracing_enabled = FALSE) – disable ‘shinyOAuth’ OpenTelemetry span creation and async trace-context propagation. Default: TRUE

  • options(shinyOAuth.otel_logging_enabled = FALSE) – disable ‘shinyOAuth’ OpenTelemetry log emission. Default: TRUE

  • options(shinyOAuth.otel_include_authorization_details = TRUE) – include raw scope names, claim targets, and ACR values in telemetry. Default: FALSE (counts only). These fields can reveal private information and produce many distinct telemetry values.

See Audit logging for R hook examples and OpenTelemetry for log and trace exporter setup.

HTTP settings (timeout, retries, user agent)

Network settings limit request duration and response size.

  • options(shinyOAuth.tls_min_version = "1.2") - require TLS 1.2 or later for package HTTPS requests (the default). Use "1.3" for a higher minimum; an absent option or NULL restores TLS 1.2. Set this before discovery or login. It applies to async workers too; browser and reverse-proxy TLS must be configured separately.

  • options(shinyOAuth.timeout = 5) – default HTTP timeout (seconds) applied to all outbound requests (discovery, JWKS, token exchange, userinfo). Increase if your provider/network is slow. Values beyond curl’s supported timeout range are capped

  • options(shinyOAuth.retry_max_tries = 3L) – maximum attempts after network errors or HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx responses. Code exchange and refresh skip automatic retries, apart from one DPoP nonce-challenge retry.

  • options(shinyOAuth.dpop_nonce_max_bytes = 4096L) – maximum DPoP nonce size in bytes; supported range 1 to 65536.

  • options(shinyOAuth.retry_backoff_base = 0.5) – base backoff in seconds used for exponential backoff with jitter

  • options(shinyOAuth.retry_backoff_cap = 5) – per‑attempt cap on backoff seconds (before jitter)

  • options(shinyOAuth.retry_after_cap = 60) – maximum synchronous sleep in seconds for a server-provided Retry-After value; this is separate from the client-side backoff cap

  • options(shinyOAuth.retry_status = c(408L, 429L, 500:599)) – HTTP statuses considered transient and retried

  • options(shinyOAuth.user_agent = "shinyOAuth/<version> R/<version> httr2/<version>") – override the HTTP User-Agent. The default includes the installed package and R versions.

  • options(shinyOAuth.allow_redirect = FALSE) – reject redirects on sensitive provider requests by default. The opt-in permits redirects in all sessions, potentially forwarding codes, tokens or credentials to another destination.

  • options(shinyOAuth.max_body_bytes = 1048576) - maximum response size (default 1 MiB) for package requests and connection calls. perform_resource_req() applies it to prepared requests as well as URLs.

Async timeout (mirai)

A task timeout limits how long background work may run. Configure workers first, as shown in Usage.

  • options(shinyOAuth.async_timeout = 10000) – per-task timeout in milliseconds for mirai async tasks. When using mirai with dispatcher (the default), timed-out tasks are automatically cancelled and resolve as a mirai error. Use NULL (the default) for no timeout, or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647. Ignored when falling back to the ‘future’ backend

Async condition replay

Background workers can return warnings and messages to the app. Turn replay off if another logging system already handles those diagnostics.

  • options(shinyOAuth.replay_async_conditions = FALSE) – when FALSE, warnings and messages captured from async workers are silently discarded instead of being re-emitted on the main R process. Default is TRUE (replay all captured conditions). Useful if worker diagnostics are too noisy or handled separately via audit_hook

Token lifetime fallback

Some providers omit the token lifetime. This fallback lets ordinary OAuth clients track expiry in that case.

  • options(shinyOAuth.default_expires_in = 3600) – fallback token lifetime (in seconds) when the provider omits expires_in from the token response

Validation and URL policy

These settings control which token responses and addresses the app accepts.

  • options(shinyOAuth.access_token_cnf = "opaque") – use "opaque" to avoid decoding access-token binding data. The compatibility default "jwt" reads cnf without signature verification.

  • options(shinyOAuth.leeway = 30) – default clock skew leeway (seconds) for ID token exp/iat/nbf checks and state payload issued_at future check

  • options(shinyOAuth.max_id_token_lifetime = 86400) – maximum ID token lifetime in seconds (exp - iat). This is an additional package check beyond the OIDC expiry check. Default 86400 (24 hours). Set to Inf to disable the check

  • options(shinyOAuth.allowed_non_https_hosts = c("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "[::1]")) - allows these hosts to use http:// in non-OIDC URL checks; it does not relax OIDC discovery

  • options(shinyOAuth.allow_insecure_oidc_loopback = TRUE) – development-only opt-in for OIDC issuer and endpoint URLs on HTTP loopback origins; production OIDC metadata URLs must use HTTPS

  • options(shinyOAuth.allowed_hosts = c()) – when non-empty, restricts accepted hosts to this list

  • options(shinyOAuth.allow_hs = TRUE) – opt‑in HMAC validation for ID tokens (HS256/HS384/HS512). Requires a strictly server‑side client_secret and exactly one HS algorithm in id_token_allowed_algs, binding the shared key to one algorithm (RFC 8725 section 3.1)

  • options(shinyOAuth.client_assertion_ttl = 120L) – lifetime in seconds for JWT client assertions used with client_secret_jwt or private_key_jwt token endpoint authentication. Finite values below 60 seconds are coerced to 60 seconds, finite values above 300 seconds are clamped to 300 seconds, and NA or non-finite values fall back to the 120-second default

  • options(shinyOAuth.state_fail_delay_ms = 0) – delay before state-validation failures, in milliseconds. Default 0 adds no delay; one positive number sets a fixed delay, two set random bounds. Positive delays block R even with async = TRUE; they add timing noise rather than constant-time validation.

allowed_hosts patterns support globs (*, ?). For example, c(".example.com") matches the domain and its subdomains; "*" accepts any host.

State store

Pending login records let the app recognize the returning browser. Shared stores must consume each record only once, even when several R processes handle requests.

  • options(shinyOAuth.allow_non_atomic_state_store = TRUE) – allow separate reads and deletes in a shared store. Default FALSE requires atomic [["take"]](). Enabling this can let concurrent requests reuse a login record; the default rejects this backend. See custom_cache().

Size caps

State envelope

  • options(shinyOAuth.state_max_token_chars = 8192) – maximum allowed length of the base64url-encoded state query parameter
  • options(shinyOAuth.state_max_wrapper_bytes = 8192) – maximum decoded byte size of the outer JSON wrapper (before parsing)
  • options(shinyOAuth.state_max_ct_b64_chars = 8192) – maximum allowed length of the base64url-encoded ciphertext inside the wrapper
  • options(shinyOAuth.state_max_ct_bytes = 8192) – maximum decoded byte size of the ciphertext before attempting AES-GCM decrypt

These limits keep oversized state parameters from using excessive CPU or memory during decoding and decryption.

Callback query

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_code_bytes = 8192) – maximum decoded authorization-code bytes. Oversized values are rejected without truncation.

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_state_bytes = 8192) – maximum byte length of the state query parameter (outer token string)

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_error_bytes = 256) – maximum byte length of the error query parameter

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_error_description_bytes = 4096) – maximum byte length of the error_description query parameter

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_error_uri_bytes = 2048) – maximum byte length of the error_uri query parameter

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_iss_bytes = 2048) – maximum byte length of the iss query parameter (RFC 9207 issuer identification)

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_query_bytes = <derived>) – maximum raw query bytes. Applies before parsing to app queries, callbacks and hosted Request Objects.

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_browser_token_bytes = 256) – maximum byte length of the browser_token argument accepted by handle_callback()

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_form_post_body_bytes = <derived>) – maximum byte length of the raw form_post callback body before parsing

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_form_post_handle_bytes = 128) – maximum byte length of the transient shinyOAuth_form_post handle query parameter

  • options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_form_post_id_bytes = 256) – maximum byte length of the transient shinyOAuth_form_post_id module-id query parameter

These limits reject oversized callback URLs and POST bodies before they cause excessive processing or logging.

Generated login state must fit both shinyOAuth.callback_max_state_bytes and the state envelope limits above. Their outer-token defaults both allow 8192 bytes (base64url state is ASCII). Lowering either limit can restrict ordinary logins with many scopes or other state metadata. prepare_call() checks both budgets before storing pending login state, publishing a Request Object, or sending PAR.

Configuration assessments

Use check_oauth21(client) to review settings without making requests or changing the app. The report separates configuration problems, recommendations and things that need deployment testing. See check_oauth21() for an example and the specification revision assessed.

Local debugging

  • options(shinyOAuth.skip_browser_token = TRUE) – skip browser cookie binding in tests or interactive sessions
  • options(shinyOAuth.skip_id_sig = TRUE) – skip ID token signature verification in tests or interactive sessions
  • options(shinyOAuth.allow_unsigned_userinfo_jwt = TRUE) – accept unsigned (alg=none) UserInfo JWTs in tests or interactive sessions; outside those contexts ‘shinyOAuth’ errors instead of honoring it
  • options(shinyOAuth.debug = TRUE) – re‑raise errors during token exchange
  • options(shinyOAuth.expose_error_body = TRUE) – enable sanitized diagnostic text for local debugging. Fields are capped at 512 UTF-8 bytes and can still contain private provider data. The option is disabled by default and takes effect only in tests or interactive sessions.

Advanced transport constraints

Response limits cover both downloaded and decoded gzip data; other encodings are rejected. Use perform_resource_req(token, request) to retain the decoded size limit, adding client for DPoP or mTLS. Direct httr2::req_perform() uses httr2’s transport settings instead.

Advanced parameter overrides

Overrides allow selected extra parameters beyond the normal client and provider arguments.

By default, shinyOAuth blocks security-critical parameters in extra_auth_params, extra_token_params, and extra_token_headers to protect state binding, PKCE and client authentication from accidental overrides.

Set the callback format with oauth_client(response_mode = ...).

  • options(shinyOAuth.unblock_auth_params = c("redirect_uri")) – allow selected authorization-parameter overrides.

  • options(shinyOAuth.unblock_token_params = c(...)) – allow selected token-exchange parameter overrides.

  • options(shinyOAuth.unblock_token_headers = c("authorization")) – allow selected token-header overrides, matched case-insensitively. Authorization and Cookie are blocked by default.
